READ-ONLY analysis in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Change nothing, create no files.

Task: harvest the PR and code-review workflow knowledge a frontend development LEAD needs for a personal playbook. I need operative rules and the reasoning behind them, with exact file:line references, not a table of contents.

Read IN FULL:
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/coderabbit.yaml
- every file under /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.coderabbit/ (including .coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/*.yml and .coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/utils/*)
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/semgrep.yml
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/scripts/hooks/* (pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push, and any others)
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.husky/* if present
- package.json scripts section (to know what `npm run test`, `lint`, `audit:tokens`, `test:max-file-size` etc. actually run)
- /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/code-quality/SKILL.md

Also run these to establish ground truth about what is ACTUALLY REQUIRED vs merely present:
- `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches/develop/protection 2>&1 | head -60` and the same for `main` (if gh is authenticated; if it 404s or errors, say so plainly and note you could not determine it)
- `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/rulesets 2>&1 | head -40` if available

REPORT, as structured markdown:
1. **Every job in qa.yml**: name, trigger condition, what it actually asserts, whether it can be skipped/conditional, and whether it is a hard gate. Pay close attention to `if:` conditions, `continue-on-error`, and any job that is conditionally skipped — a skipped required check counts as PASSING in GitHub, so call out any job whose skip path silently green-lights a PR.
2. **CodeRabbit config**: what it reviews, what path filters/exclusions exist, what it is configured to enforce (commit format, Tier 1 detection, ast-grep rules, semgrep), and whether CodeRabbit is a blocking gate or advisory.
3. **Each ast-grep rule and each semgrep rule**: what pattern it catches, and — importantly — what closely-related mistake it does NOT catch (the evasion/blind spot).
4. **Git hooks**: what each hook blocks locally, and how it is bypassed (`--no-verify`), i.e. which of these are prevention vs. best-effort.
5. **The manual, human-only steps**: what a developer must do that NO tool will catch — e.g. running `cr review --light --base develop` locally, replying in-thread to every CodeRabbit finding, running `npm run audit:tokens`, tsc/lint if ungated. Be specific about which quality checks have NO CI gate at all.
6. **"What bites you"**: 5-10 specific non-obvious traps for a lead.

Be explicit about anything you could not determine. Cite file:line for every claim.

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files.     24	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

   338	        env:

   340	          # @salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime's getConfig() reads to pick
   341	          # config/<target>.js — must be a real process env var before
   342	          # `pwa-kit-dev start` launches, since getConfig() resolves it
   343	          # before config/default.js's own .env-loading code ever runs.

   353	          COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE }}
   354	          COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID }}

    20	
    21	reviews:
    22	  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
    23	  high_level_summary: true
    24	
    25	  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
    26	  poem: false
    27	
    28	  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
    29	  collapse_walkthrough: false
    30	
    31	  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
    32	  request_changes_workflow: true
    33	
    34	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    35	  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
    36	  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
    37	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    38	  profile: "assertive"
    39	
    40	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    41	  # PATH FILTERS — excludes mechanically-generated/derived files from
    42	  # review scope entirely (distinct from path_instructions above, which
    43	  # only changes review *criteria*, not whether a file is reviewed at
    44	  # all). These files are regenerated from other source files already
    45	  # covered by path_instructions/code_guidelines below — reviewing the
    46	  # derived copy too is redundant, and scripts/hooks/pre-commit already
    47	  # blocks hand-editing them directly, so review findings on them can't
    48	  # be actioned there anyway. Excluding lock files per CodeRabbit's own
    49	  # recommendation (docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/review-instructions).
    50	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    51	  path_filters:
    52	    - "!package-lock.json"
    53	    # Generated by scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs from .claude/rules/*.md + AGENTS.md
    54	    - "!.cursor/rules/**"
    55	    - "!.vscode/instructions/**"
    56	    - "!.github/copilot-instructions.md"
    57	    # Generated by scripts/generateRegistry.mjs from overrides/app/
    58	    - "!.claude/registry/*.md"
    59	    # f2r/ is a self-contained design-prototyping/handover toolkit with its own
    60	    # governance (f2r/AGENTS.md, f2r/CLAUDE.md) — per this repo's AGENTS.md Hard
    61	    # Rule 16, its own rules apply inside it, not this file's. It ships neither
    62	    # to the storefront nor to production, so it's out of scope for a storefront
    63	    # PR review; excluded here rather than reviewed against criteria (SSR safety,
    64	    # Chakra tokens, multi-region, etc.) that don't apply to it.
    65	    - "!f2r/**"
    66	
    67	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    68	  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
    69	  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
    70	  # Different review instructions per file path.
    71	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    72	  path_instructions:
    73	    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
    74	    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
    75	    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
    76	    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
    77	    - path: "overrides/**"
    78	      instructions: |
    79	        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
    80	        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
    81	        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
    82	        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.
    83	
    84	        For every PR, check:
    85	
    86	        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
    87	           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.
    88	
    89	        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
    90	           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
    91	           complete page breakdowns.
    92	
    93	        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
    94	           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
    95	           cause stale data that persists until page reload.
    96	
    97	        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
    98	           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
    99	           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.
   100

content.content:
1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# Pre-commit hook:
     3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
     4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
     5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
     6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
     7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
     8	#
     9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
    10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
    11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
    12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
    14	
    15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
    17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
    18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
    19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
    20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21	
    22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
    24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
    25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
    26	
    27	  # fnm
    28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
    29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
    30	  fi
    31	
    32	  # volta
    33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
    35	  fi
    36	
    37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
    38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
    39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
    40	    exit 1
    41	  fi
    42	fi
    43	
    44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
    46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
    47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48	
    49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
    50	
    51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
    52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
    53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
    54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
    55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
    56	
    57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
    58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
    59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
    60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
    61	  git add .claude/registry/
    62	fi
    63	
    64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
    66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
    67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
    68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
    69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    70	
    71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
    72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    74	    || true)
    75	
    76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    78	    if ! node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null; then
    79	      echo ""
    80	      echo "  ❌  sync:ai-rules:fix failed — derived AI config files may be stale or partially"
    81	      echo "      written. Fix the error above, then re-stage and commit again."
    82	      echo ""
    83	      exit 1
    84	    fi
    85	    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
    86	  fi
    87	fi
    88	
    89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    90	# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
    91	#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
    92	#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
    93	#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
    94	#     automatically.
    95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    96	
    97	skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    98	  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
    99	  || true)
   100	
   101	if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
   102	  echo ""
   103	  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
   104	  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'
   105	
   106	  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
   107	    echo ""
   108	    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
   109	    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
   110	  fi
   111	
   112	  echo ""
   113	  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
   114	  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
   115	  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
   116	  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
   117	  echo ""
   118	fi
   119	
   120	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   121	# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
   122	#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
   123	#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
   124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125	
   126	experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
   127	  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
   128	  || true)
   129	
   130	if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
   131	  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."
   132	
   133	  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
   134	  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
   135	  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT
   136	
   137	  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
   138	  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
   139	  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
   140	  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
   141	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   142	    name=$(basename "$f")
   143	    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
   144	    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
   145	      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
   146	    else
   147	      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
   148	    fi
   149	  done
   150	
   151	  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
   152	    echo ""
   153	    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
   154	    exit 1
   155	  fi
   156	
   157	  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
   158	  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
   159	  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
   160	fi
   161	
   162	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   163	# 3. Derived configuration file guard
   164	#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
   165	#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
   166	#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
   167	#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
   168	#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
   169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   170	
   171	blocked_files=()
   172	
   173	# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
   174	modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)
   175	
   176	while IFS= read -r file; do
   177	  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
   178	
   179	  # Only check files in derived locations
   180	  case "$file" in
   181	    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
   182	    *) continue ;;
   183	  esac
   184	
   185	  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
   186	  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
   187	  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
   188	  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue
   189	
   190	  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
   191	  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
   192	  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
   193	    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
   194	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')
   195	
   196	  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue
   197	
   198	  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
   199	  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
   200	  # Skip it.
   201	  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
   202	  any_source_staged=false
   203	  while IFS= read -r src; do
   204	    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
   205	    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
   206	    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
   207	      any_source_staged=true
   208	      break
   209	    fi
   210	  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
   211	  if $any_source_staged; then
   212	    continue
   213	  fi
   214	
   215	  # Fall back to the same AI-sources trigger condition step 1b uses to decide
   216	  # whether to regenerate this file in the first place. A derived file's own
   217	  # synced-from header may not yet list every source that legitimately feeds
   218	  # it (e.g. a skill file added after the header was last written) — if step
   219	  # 1b would have regenerated this file because a .claude/rules/*.md or
   220	  # .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md file is staged, that is also a legitimate sync,
   221	  # not a direct edit.
   222	  if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qE '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$'; then
   223	    continue
   224	  fi
   225	
   226	  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
   227	  blocked_files+=("$file")
   228	
   229	done <<< "$modified_staged"
   230	
   231	if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
   232	  echo ""
   233	  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
   234	  echo ""
   235	  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
   236	    echo "       $bf"
   237	  done
   238	  echo ""
   239	  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
   240	  echo ""
   241	  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
   242	  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
   243	  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
   244	  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
   245	  echo ""
   246	  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
   247	  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
   248	  echo ""
   249	  exit 1
   250	fi
   251	
   252	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   253	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
   254	#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
   255	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
   256	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
   257	#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
   258	#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
   259	#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
   260	#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
   261	#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
   262	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   263	
   264	if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
   265	  secret_violations=()
   266	
   267	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   268	    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
   269	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
   270	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
   271	    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
   272	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   273	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
   274	
   275	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
   276	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
   277	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
   278	      continue
   279	    fi
   280	
   281	    # Value looks like a JWT
   282	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
   283	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
   284	      continue
   285	    fi
   286	
   287	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
   288	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
   289	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
   290	      continue
   291	    fi
   292	
   293	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
   294	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
   295	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
   296	      continue
   297	    fi

   299	    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
   300	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then

   318	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
   319	    echo ""
   320	    exit 1
   321	  fi

=====.husky/pre-commit=====
     1	bash scripts/hooks/pre-commit
=====.husky/commit-msg=====

=====.husky/pre-push=====

=====scripts/hooks/README.md=====
     1	# Git hooks
     2	
     3	Two hooks ship in this folder:
     4	
     5	- **`pre-commit`** — regenerates `.claude/registry/`, warns on Contentful definition drift, blocks direct edits to derived AI-config files (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) when their `.claude/` source is not also staged, warns when a skill (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`) changes without `.claude/skills/README.md` also staged and reminds to update the mirrored Confluence page (no automated push exists yet), and **blocks** any commit where `.env.sample` has a non-empty value for a variable whose name looks like a secret (`TOKEN`/`SECRET`/`KEY`/`PASSWORD`/`CREDENTIAL`) — real values belong only in `.env` (gitignored).
     6	- **`commit-msg`** — enforces conventional commits (`type(scope): description`). Allowed types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `upstream-sync`.
     7	
     8	## Install
     9	
    10	Husky wires these in automatically on `npm install` via the `prepare` script in `package.json`. The Husky-managed wrappers live in [`.husky/pre-commit`](../../.husky/pre-commit) and [`.husky/commit-msg`](../../.husky/commit-msg) and just delegate to the scripts here.
    11	
    12	If Husky did not install (e.g. cloned with `--no-install` or hooks are not running), install manually:
    13	
    14	```bash
    15	cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit  .git/hooks/pre-commit  && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    16	cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg  .git/hooks/commit-msg  && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
    17	```
    18	
    19	## Bypass
    20	
    21	Hooks should not be bypassed. If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue rather than running `git commit --no-verify` — see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) hard rule 13.
=====scripts/hooks/commit-msg=====
     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
     3	#
     4	# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
     5	#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
     6	
     7	commit_msg=$(cat "$1")
     8	
     9	# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
    10	if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
    11	  exit 0
    12	fi
    13	
    14	# Conventional commits pattern
    15	# type(optional-scope): description
    16	# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
    17	pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
    18	
    19	if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
    20	  echo ""
    21	  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
    22	  echo ""
    23	  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
    24	  echo ""
    25	  echo "  Types:"
    26	  echo "    feat           new feature"
    27	  echo "    fix            bug fix"
    28	  echo "    docs           documentation only"
    29	  echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
    30	  echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
    31	  echo "    perf           performance improvement"
    32	  echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
    33	  echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
    34	  echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
    35	  echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
    36	  echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
    37	  echo ""

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# pre-push — reject malformed version tags (v*) before they leave this machine.
     3	#
     4	# Why this exists: on the GitHub Team plan, repository-ruleset `tag_name_pattern`
     5	# rules are NOT enforced (they are an Enterprise-only feature), so this client-side
     6	# hook is the primary *prevention* for tag naming. The `tag-validate.yml` workflow is
     7	# the post-push safety net (it can only flag, not block, since it runs after the push).
     8	#
     9	# Allowed:   vX.Y.Z-rc.N      (release candidate)
    10	#            vX.Y.Z           (final)
    11	#            vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N  (hotfix)
    12	# Untouched: any non-v* tag (e.g. sprint/*, sit/deploy/*) and all branch pushes.
    13	#
    14	# git passes the refs being pushed on stdin as:
    15	#   <local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>
    16	# Key on the REMOTE ref — that's the ref being created on the remote, so it also
    17	# catches `git push origin <branch>:refs/tags/vX` where the local ref isn't a tag.
    18	# A deletion has local_ref == "(delete)"; skip those (tag deletion is governed by
    19	# the ruleset and must not be blocked here).
    20	rc_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-rc\.[0-9]+$'
    21	final_re='^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-hotfix\.[0-9]+)?$'
    22	status=0
    23	
    24	while read -r local_ref _lsha remote_ref _rsha; do
    25	  case "$remote_ref" in
    26	    refs/tags/v*)
    27	      tag=${remote_ref#refs/tags/}
    28	      if [[ "$local_ref" != "(delete)" ]] && [[ ! $tag =~ $rc_re && ! $tag =~ $final_re ]]; then
    29	        echo "✗ pre-push: refusing malformed version tag '$tag'" >&2
    30	        echo "  allowed: vX.Y.Z-rc.N | vX.Y.Z | vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N" >&2
    31	        status=1
    32	      fi
    33	      ;;
    34	  esac
    35	done
    36	
    37	exit $status

input.command: echo "=====code-quality SKILL====="; cat -n .claude/skills/code-quality/SKILL.md

content.content:
=====code-quality SKILL=====
     1	---
     2	name: code-quality
     3	description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
     4	---
     5	
     6	Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
     7	diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Input
    12	
    13	The user will provide one of:
    14	- A file path or directory to audit
    15	- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`
    16	
    17	If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
    18	Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## Parallel execution
    23	
    24	For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
    25	as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
    26	bundle all checks into one agent.
    27	
    28	- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
    29	- **Agent B — Import analysis**
    30	- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
    31	- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**
    32	
    33	For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.
    34	
    35	---
    36	
    37	## Agent A — Naming & structure
    38	
    39	Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
    40	(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
    41	[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
    42	ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
    43	that's how the files drift apart.
    44	
    45	Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:
    46	
    47	- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
    48	- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
    49	- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
    50	  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
    51	  structure**.
    52	- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
    53	- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.
    54	
    55	For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
    56	anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").
    57	
    58	---
    59	
    60	## Agent B — Import analysis
    61	
    62	For each file, read the import statements and check:
    63	
    64	- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
    65	  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
    66	- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
    67	  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
    68	  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
    69	- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
    70	- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	## Agent C — TypeScript coverage
    75	
    76	Check each file against the relevant rule file:
    77	
    78	- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
    79	  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
    80	  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
    81	- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
    82	  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
    83	- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
    84	  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).
    85	
    86	Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
    87	errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.
    88	
    89	---
    90	
    91	## Agent D — Test & story coverage
    92	
    93	For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
    94	- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
    95	- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
    96	  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
    97	  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
    98	  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
    99	  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
   100	  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
   101	  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
   102	- If a test file exists, verify:
   103	  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
   104	  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
   105	  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
   106	- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
   107	- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
   108	  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.
   109	
   110	For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
   111	- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
   112	  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
   113	  one-liners are exempt.
   114	- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
   115	  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).
   116	
   117	---
   118	
   119	## Output format
   120	
   121	Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:
   122	
   123	```
   124	## Code Quality Report
   125	**Scope:** [files audited]
   126	**Branch:** [current branch]
   127	**Date:** [today]
   128	
   129	### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
   130	[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]
   131	
   132	### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
   133	[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]
   134	
   135	### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
   136	[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]
   137	
   138	### ✅ No issues found
   139	[List checks that passed cleanly]
   140	
   141	### Summary
   142	X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
   143	```
   144	
   145	Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
   146	Do not modify any files — report only.

=== deploy-preview triggers ===
     1	name: Deploy Preview
     2	
     3	# Ephemeral per-branch MRT preview environments. On every push to a feature/fix
     4	# branch, creates (or reuses) a dedicated MRT environment, syncs runtime env vars,
     5	# builds, and deploys — giving devs/testers a live URL to review during PR without
     6	# waiting for a merge to develop. Companion teardown workflow: teardown-preview.yml.
     7	#
     8	# Every ephemeral target is prefixed `pr-`, so it can never collide with the fixed
     9	# named environments (dev, dev1, test, sit, stg, uat, production).
    10	
    11	on:
    12	  push:
    13	    branches:
    14	      - 'feature/**'
    15	      - 'fix/**'
    16	      - '!fix/release-*'
    17	      # `*` doesn't match `/` in GitHub Actions branch globs, so the pattern
    18	      # above alone wouldn't exclude a nested fix/release/<version> naming slip
    19	      # — this repo's documented convention is the hyphenated
    20	      # fix/release-{version}-* form, but this guards defensively either way.
    21	      - '!fix/release/**'
    22	
    23	# Keyed on the raw branch name (not the derived slug) — concurrency groups are
    24	# evaluated before any job/step runs, so the key can't depend on a step output.
    25	# cancel-in-progress is deliberately false: a cancelled Actions run does NOT cancel
    26	# an already-submitted MRT-side operation (a POST/PATCH, or an in-flight
    27	# `pwa-kit-dev push`), so a naively-cancelled run's server-side effects could still
    28	# land after its successor starts. Same reasoning deploy-test.yml documents for its
    29	# own cancel-in-progress: false.
    30	concurrency:
    31	  group: mrt-preview-${{ github.ref_name }}
    32	  cancel-in-progress: false
    33	
    34	permissions:
    35	  contents: read
    36	  pull-requests: write
    37	
    38	jobs:
    39	  deploy-preview:
    40	    name: Deploy Preview

=== teardown-preview triggers ===
     1	name: Teardown Preview
     2	
     3	# Companion to deploy-preview.yml. Deletes the ephemeral MRT environment for a
     4	# branch once it's no longer needed.
     5	#
     6	# Two triggers are both necessary: `pull_request: closed` covers the normal PR
     7	# merge/close path, and `delete` is a backstop for a branch deleted without ever
     8	# opening a PR. This repo has delete_branch_on_merge enabled, so a normal merge
     9	# fires BOTH events for the same branch, usually seconds apart — every step below
    10	# is written to be safe under that double-fire, not just under the concurrency
    11	# group serialising them.
    12	
    13	on:
    14	  # No `branches:` filter — a preview PR closing against any base (not just
    15	  # develop) must still tear down its target, or a PR opened against the wrong
    16	  # base leaves an MRT target running with only the `delete` backstop to catch
    17	  # it. resolve-branch's eligibility check below already filters by head branch
    18	  # pattern, which is the check that actually matters here.
    19	  pull_request:
    20	    types: [closed]
    21	  delete:
    22	
    23	permissions:
    24	  contents: read
    25	  pull-requests: write
    26	
    27	jobs:
    28	  # `on.delete` has no branch-filter syntax (fires for tag deletions too), and
    29	  # `on.pull_request.branches` filters by base branch, not head branch — neither
    30	  # trigger can express "head/deleted branch matches feature/**|fix/** but not

=== auditTokenUsage.mjs header (first 60 lines) ===
     1	#!/usr/bin/env node
     2	/**
     3	 * Token usage audit — flags a raw hex colour / px / rem / em literal in an override component
     4	 * or theme recipe, where a Zimmermann token (a foundation constant, a var(--zimm-*) reference,
     5	 * or a Chakra prop resolving through a registered scale) should be used instead.
     6	 *
     7	 * Usage:
     8	 *   node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
     9	 *
    10	 * Scope: overrides/app/components/** and overrides/app/theme/components/** — .ts/.tsx/.scss.
    11	 * Deliberately excludes:
    12	 *   - overrides/app/theme/foundation/ — not under either scan root; these files ARE the source
    13	 *     of truth, so a raw value there is the point, not a violation.
    14	 *   - *.test.ts(x) and *.stories.tsx — test assertions and Storybook demo code routinely need
    15	 *     illustrative/representative raw values that aren't "a hardcoded design value shipped to
    16	 *     production" in the sense this audit cares about (testing.md already treats these
    17	 *     differently from production styling rigor).
    18	 *
    19	 * A match is downgraded from a failure to an ACKNOWLEDGED exception (still printed, does not
    20	 * affect the exit code) when the contiguous non-blank block of lines ending at the match — i.e.
    21	 * the match's own line plus every line above it up to the nearest blank line or file start —
    22	 * contains "provisional", "pending", "placeholder", or an explicit "audit-allow". This is the
    23	 * exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for every documented raw-value exception today
    24	 * (e.g. zimmButton.css.ts's BTN_HEIGHT_LG/BTN_HEIGHT_SM/BTN_PADDING_Y, footer.css.ts's
    25	 * SPACE_SECTION/SIZE_COL_SUB/SIZE_COL_MAP). Reading the existing explanatory comment as the
    26	 * allow-list entry avoids a second, separately-maintained list that would drift from the code
    27	 * the moment either one changes.
    28	 *
    29	 * The "nearest blank line" boundary, not a fixed line count, matters: this codebase's real
    30	 * exception comments are often a shared multi-line block covering several sibling declarations
    31	 * (footer.css.ts's four provisional constants share one comment), or wrap the marker word
    32	 * itself across a line break (zimmSubscribeSection.css.ts had "...52/40. Pending\n// Kiera."
    33	 * — "Pending" and "Kiera" on different lines). A fixed N-line window missed both shapes during
    34	 * this script's own first calibration pass against the real codebase.
    35	 *
    36	 * This is a line-based grep, not an AST parse — matches
    37	 * .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's own framing ("it greps for exactly this"). A real
    38	 * false-positive class this cannot fully rule out: a hex-looking string in a non-colour
    39	 * context (e.g. a URL fragment that happens to be 3-8 hex characters) would still be flagged;
    40	 * mark it with `// audit-allow: <reason>` rather than trying to make the regex smarter.
    41	 *
    42	 * Not wired into CI yet — see overrideStyling.md's note on why (someone needs to own triaging
    43	 * false positives on a real run first).
    44	 */
    45	
    46	import { readFileSync, readdirSync, existsSync } from 'fs';
    47	import { join, extname, relative, dirname } from 'path';
    48	import { fileURLToPath } from 'url';
    49	
    50	const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
    51	const ROOT = join(__dirname, '..');
    52	const APP = join(ROOT, 'overrides/app');
    53	
    54	const SCAN_ROOTS = [join(APP, 'components'), join(APP, 'theme/components')];
    55	const SCAN_EXTENSIONS = new Set(['.ts', '.tsx', '.scss']);
    56	
    57	const HEX_RE = /#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b/g;
    58	const UNIT_RE = /\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:rem|em|px)\b/g;
    59	const EXCEPTION_MARKER_RE = /provisional|pending|placeholder|audit-allow/i;
    60

I have complete ground truth. Writing up the findings. --- # PR & Code-Review Playbook — Zimmermann PWA Ground truth established live against `ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa` on 2026-08-25 as `marcelannavarro`. All three branch-protection rules, both rulesets, and a real merged PR (#59) were readable. ## 0. The merge gate, as GitHub actually enforces it Source: `gh api graphql branchProtectionRules` (verified, not inferred). | Branch | Required status checks | Approvals | Code-owner review | Admin-enforced | Stale reviews dismissed | Conversation resolution required | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `develop` | `Unit tests (Vitest)`, `Storybook interaction & a11y tests`, `🔴 Branch Target Check` | 1 | yes | yes | **yes** | **no** | | `main` | `🔴 Branch Target Check` **only** | 1 | yes | yes | no | **no** | | `release/**` | `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `SIT Gate` | 1 | yes | yes | no | **no** | Four things a lead must internalise from this table: 1. **`Playwright E2E (localhost)` and `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` are NOT required checks on any branch.** They can fail red and the PR still merges. Only Vitest + Storybook + Branch Target gate `develop`. 2. **`main` has no test gate at all.** A `release/*` → `main` PR is gated on one job that only checks the branch name pair, plus one code-owner approval. 3. **`requiresConversationResolution: false` on all three branches.** AGENTS.md's "always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every CodeRabbit finding" is *entirely* honour-system. Nothing blocks a merge with 30 unanswered CodeRabbit threads. 4. **`requireLastPushApproval: false` everywhere, and `dismissesStaleReviews: false` on `main` and `release/**`.** On a release or hotfix branch you can get your approval, then push arbitrary new commits, and merge without re-review. Only `develop` dismisses stale approvals. This is the inverse of what you'd want — the highest-risk branches have the weakest post-approval protection. Rulesets (`gh api .../rulesets`) contain **only two tag rulesets** — `tag-rc` (20487306) and `tag-release` (20487243), both `target: tag`. There are no branch rulesets; all branch enforcement is via the legacy branch-protection API above. This corroborates `.claude/rules/tagging.md`'s claim that tag *naming* is inert on the Team plan. --- ## 1. Every job in `qa.yml` Trigger for the whole workflow: `pull_request` to `develop` or `release/**` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml:3-7`). It does **not** run on `main`-targeted PRs. ### `detect-changes` — "Detect relevant changes" (`qa.yml:25`) - **Trigger:** always (no `if:`). - **Asserts:** nothing. It computes four outputs (`qa.yml:30-35`) that gate every other job. - **Hard gate?** No — not a required check. **But it is the single point of failure for the two that are.** - **The critical mechanism** is `since_last_remote_commit: true` (`qa.yml:72`). The diff is against **the previous push on the PR branch**, not the merge-base with `develop`. The comment at `qa.yml:59-71` explains the intent (stop a docs-only follow-up re-triggering suites for the PR's life) and explicitly acknowledges the semantics at `qa.yml:22-23`: *"GitHub treats a skipped required check as passing."* - Note the asymmetry at `qa.yml:31-33`: `vitest` and `e2e` OR in `runtime_changed`; `storybook` does not. - `Compute E2E scope` (`qa.yml:113-147`) narrows E2E to one area only if **every** e2e-relevant changed file is in that area's allow-list; a single file outside falls back to `full` (`qa.yml:139-146`). Only **one** area is defined — `e2e_homepage` (`qa.yml:97-102`) — despite `.claude/rules/testing.md` listing seven. - `Detect Jira story keys` (`qa.yml:158-167`) regexes `SFCC-\d+` out of PR title, body, and branch name. ### `unit-tests` — "Unit tests (Vitest)" (`qa.yml:207`) — **REQUIRED on `develop`** - **Trigger:** `if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'` (`qa.yml:211`). - **Asserts:** `npm test` = `vitest run` (`package.json:45`), which runs `overrides/**/*.test.ts(x)` (`vitest.config.ts:11`). **22 test files exist.** `vitest.config.ts` has **no coverage block and no thresholds** — so "passes" means "the 22 files that exist don't fail," not that anything is covered. - **Skippable?** Yes — whenever nothing under `overrides/**`, `vitest.config.*`, `vitest.setup.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, or `babel.config.js` changed *since the last push* (`qa.yml:103-108`). - **Hard gate?** Nominally yes, practically conditional. **A skip reports green.** ### `storybook-test` — "Storybook interaction & a11y tests" (`qa.yml:236`) — **REQUIRED on `develop`** - **Trigger:** `if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'` (`qa.yml:240`). - **Asserts:** builds Storybook, serves it, runs `test-storybook --ci` (`qa.yml:255-262`) — `play()` functions plus `@storybook/addon-a11y` checks. This is **the only automated accessibility gate in the entire PR pipeline.** - **Skippable?** Yes. Its path list (`qa.yml:80-88`) covers `components/`, `pages/`, `hooks/`, `theme/`, `types/`, `.storybook/`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` — and **omits `overrides/app/utils/**` and `overrides/app/config/**`**. A change to a util that a component renders through gets no a11y run. - **Hard gate?** Same as above — skip reports green. ### `e2e-localhost` — "Playwright E2E (localhost)" (`qa.yml:280`) — **NOT required** - **Trigger:** `!cancelled() && e2e == 'true' && (unit-tests success or skipped)` (`qa.yml:313-316`). - **Asserts:** boots `npm start` against the real SFCC dev org, waits for the literal string `webpack built client` in the log (`qa.yml:367-373`), runs Chromium + mobile-chrome, scoped by `e2e_scope` (`qa.yml:379-384`). - `timeout-minutes: 15` (`qa.yml:299`), bound to the `dev` GitHub Environment (`qa.yml:290`). - **Hard gate?** **No.** Not in any required-context list. Red Playwright does not block merge. ### `e2e-browserstack` — "Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)" (`qa.yml:427`) — **NOT required** - **Trigger:** `always() && e2e == 'true' && (unit-tests success or skipped) && (base is release/** OR jira_keys != '')` (`qa.yml:432-436`). - **Asserts:** full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite on `release/**`; otherwise `--grep` scoped to the PR's `@SFCC-NNN` tags (`qa.yml:454-460`). - **No Jira key in title/body/branch → the job never runs.** Deliberate, per `qa.yml:420-425`. - **Hard gate?** No. ### Bug worth knowing: the `always()` / `!cancelled()` mismatch `qa.yml:431` comments *"Same always()/skipped handling as e2e-localhost above"* — but line 433 uses `always()` while `e2e-localhost` uses `!cancelled()` (`qa.yml:314`). The comment at `qa.yml:309-312` explains precisely why `!cancelled()` was chosen: to avoid burning a runner on a superseded run. `e2e-browserstack` does not inherit that fix, so a superseded push still spins up **paid BrowserStack sessions**. The comment asserts a parity that does not exist in the code. ### What `qa.yml` does NOT contain Verified by grep across `.github/workflows/`: **there is no `npm run lint` job, no `npx tsc --noEmit` job, no `npm run audit:tokens` job, and no bundle-size job in `qa.yml`.** `test:max-file-size` appears only in `deploy-dev.yml:50`, `deploy-test.yml:110`, and `digital-sit.yml:134` — all post-merge or release-tier. Lighthouse appears only in `digital-sit.yml:68`. ### Other workflows that fire on a PR - `protected-file-guard.yml` — see §5 below. - `deploy-preview.yml` — triggers on **push** to `feature/**`/`fix/**` (`:11-21`), not on `pull_request`; posts a live MRT preview URL. - `teardown-preview.yml` — `pull_request: closed` + `delete` (`:19-21`). On PR #59 this check reported **`fail`** and the PR merged anyway; it is not required. - `digital-sit.yml` "SIT Gate" — `push`/`pull_request` on `release/**` only (`:3-9`). Its `sit-gate` summary job (`:136-155`) uses `if: always()` and explicitly compares all four `needs.*.result` to `success`, so it cannot be skip-passed. **This is the best-constructed gate in the repo** — and it is the only required check that behaves the way people assume the others do. --- ## 2. CodeRabbit configuration `coderabbit.yaml`, 499 lines. Tier 1 (`CODEOWNERS:74`, `frozenFiles.md` Governance). **Posture:** `profile: "assertive"` (`:38`), `request_changes_workflow: true` (`:32`), `high_level_summary: true` (`:23`), `poem: false` (`:26`). **Scope / exclusions** — `path_filters` (`:51-65`) contains *only* negations, so everything not listed is reviewed. Excluded: `package-lock.json`, `.cursor/rules/**`, `.vscode/instructions/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.claude/registry/*.md`, and `f2r/**`. **Auto-review triggers** (`:384-393`): enabled, incremental on every push, **`drafts: false`**, and `ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]`. **Path instructions** (`:72-350`) — 20 entries. The repo-wide baseline is scoped to `overrides/**` (`:77`) and carries 12 numbered rules (`:86-135`): TypeScript-only, SSR safety guards, React Query invalidation, Chakra tokens, locale/`useIntl`, multi-region, Einstein/DataCloud events, WCAG 2.2 AA, performance, no console logs, **Claude Code provenance scrutiny (`:125-127`)**, and **conventional commits on every commit in the PR (`:129-135`)**. Then per-path entries for Tier 1 tokens (`:138`), the four critical hooks (`:155`, `:166`, `:176`, `:186`), `config/**` (`:197`), `mobify.config.js` (`:208`), `.github/workflows/**` (`:218`), `ssr.js` (`:229`), header (`:241`), `routes.tsx` (`:252`), product-tile (`:265`), display-price (`:277`), checkout (`:288`), PDP (`:301`), PLP (`:312`), `e2e/features/**` (`:323`), and `hooks/**` (`:341`). **Static-analysis tools it runs** (`:355-379`): `eslint`, `gitleaks`, `ast-grep` (rule_dirs `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules`, util_dirs `.../utils`, `essential_rules: true`), `osvScanner`, `reactDoctor`, `semgrep` with `config_file: semgrep.yml`. **Pre-merge checks** (`:399-430`): `title` **error** (conventional commits), `description` **error**, custom check *"Docstring convention compliance"* **error** (`:420-430`, scoped to shared components ≥2 callers / exported hooks / non-obvious utils), `issue_assessment` **warning** (Jira Forge app not installed, `:414-416`), blunt `docstrings` **off** (`:404-405`). **Knowledge base** (`:449-482`): Jira `SFCC` (only once the Forge app is installed — **link issues by pasting the URL into the PR body; there is no branch-name auto-detection**, `:451-455`). `code_guidelines.filePatterns` explicitly loads `AGENTS.md` plus seven `.claude/rules/*.md` files with `applyTo` scopes — the comment at `:462-465` is important: **CodeRabbit reads literal file content and does not follow AGENTS.md's markdown links**, so a rule file not listed here is invisible to review. `overrideStyling.md` and `tagging.md` are **not** in that list. ### Is CodeRabbit a blocking gate? **Split answer, and this is the nuance a lead needs.** - **As a status check: no.** The check named `CodeRabbit` appeared on PR #59 (`gh pr checks 59`) but is absent from every branch's `requiredStatusCheckContexts`. Its `mode: error` pre-merge checks therefore do not block via the status-check path. - **As a reviewer: effectively yes.** `request_changes_workflow: true` makes CodeRabbit submit a formal *Changes requested* review, and with `requiredApprovingReviewCount: 1` in force, GitHub blocks the merge button while that review stands. On PR #59 it cleared itself: *"Approve command performed: Comments resolved. Approval completed."* - **Dismissal is restricted.** On `develop`, `dismissal_restrictions.users` = `[HardiAcn]` — only that account can dismiss reviews. No such restriction on `main` or `release/**`. - **Unresolved threads never block** (`requiresConversationResolution: false` on all three branches). --- ## 3. Rule-by-rule: what each catches, and what it misses ### ast-grep — all three are `severity: warning`, so all three are review comments, not failures **`img-missing-alt`** (`.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/img-missing-alt.yml:6-14`) — any JSX element whose name matches `^img$` with no attribute matching `^alt\b`. > **Blind spot:** the regex is anchored lowercase-only. This is a **Chakra UI v2** codebase, where the idiomatic element is ``, not `` — and ``, ``, and any `` wrapper are all invisible to this rule. Also `alt={undefined}` and `alt={maybeUndefinedVar}` satisfy the check textually while producing no accessible name at runtime; conversely `{...imgProps}` carrying a real `alt` is flagged as a false positive. **`icon-button-missing-aria-label`** (`.../icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml:6-14`) — name matching `^IconButton` (prefix, so `IconButtonWithRegistration` is correctly caught) without `^aria-label\b`. > **Blind spot, and it's a nasty one:** `\b` after `label` requires a non-word character next. In `aria-labelledby` the next character is `l`, so **`aria-labelledby` does not satisfy the rule** — a correct, spec-compliant a11y pattern gets flagged as a violation. In the other direction, an aliased import (`import {IconButton as IB}` → ``), a differently-named wrapper (`ZimmIconButton`), or an icon-only `` all evade entirely. **`clickable-non-interactive-element`** (`.../clickable-non-interactive-element.yml:6-18`) — a fixed list (`div|span|Box|Flex|Stack|VStack|HStack|Grid|Text|PopoverFooter|PopoverHeader`) with an `onClick` attribute and no `role`. > **Blind spots, three of them.** (a) The element list is closed; `Center`, `SimpleGrid`, `GridItem`, `Container`, `Card`, `Wrap`, `li`, `td`, `section`, `Heading`, `Badge`, `Tag` all evade. (b) It checks only for the *presence* of `role` — `role="presentation"` and `role="none"`, which are the exact opposite of correct, satisfy it. (c) `.claude/rules/components.md` requires `role` **plus `tabIndex={0}` plus `onKeyDown`**; the rule checks none of the latter two, so `
` with zero keyboard support passes the machine check and still fails WCAG. Also `onMouseDown`/`onPointerDown` evade. `utils/jsx-element.yml:4-7` defines the shared `jsxElement` util as `jsx_opening_element` OR `jsx_self_closing_element` — correct, covers both forms. Note `essential_rules: true` (`coderabbit.yaml:368`) means CodeRabbit *also* runs its own built-in ast-grep packs on top of these three. ### semgrep — both `severity: ERROR`, both `languages: [typescript]` **`payment-credential-logged`** (`semgrep.yml:5-26`) — taint mode. Sources: a function parameter (`:15-18`) or a `const` declaration (`:20-23`) whose name matches `(?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)`. Sinks: `console.$METHOD(...)` and `Sentry.$METHOD(...)` (`:25-26`). > **Blind spots — the sink list is the big one.** `.claude/rules/conventions.md` bans these values from *"any `console.*` call, Sentry breadcrumb/event, GTM dataLayer push, analytics event, MRT access log, or response body"* and from `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/IndexedDB/cookies and query strings. **Only two of those are sinks.** `dataLayer.push({cvv})`, `localStorage.setItem('pin', pin)`, `logger.info(cvv)`, a `fetch()` query string, and a returned response body all pass clean. > **Source blind spots:** `let`/`var` are not sources (only `const`). Property access — `formData.cvv`, `card.cardNumber` — is not a source. Destructuring (`const {cvv} = form`) does not bind `$VAR` to an identifier. And the name list misses **`cvc`**, the Visa/Mastercard spelling, plus `securityCode`. Aliasing the sink (`const log = console.log; log(cvv)`) evades. > **False-positive risk:** the regex is unanchored substring, so `spinner`, `pinned`, `pinnedItems` all match `pin`. **`dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized`** (`semgrep.yml:28-35`) — matches the JSX attribute form and excludes anything of shape `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`. > **Blind spot, evasion side:** any object property spread evades — `
`, `const props = {...};
`, or `React.createElement('div', {dangerouslySetInnerHTML:{__html: dirty}})`. And the exclusion matches *any* receiver with a `.sanitize()` method, so a no-op `noop.sanitize(dirty)` passes. > **Blind spot, false-positive side — this one will bite daily:** the exclusion requires the sanitizer call to be **inline in the JSX**. The normal, correct pattern — > ```tsx > const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty) > return
> ``` > — does not match `pattern-not`, so **properly sanitized code gets flagged as an XSS ERROR.** So does `sanitizeHtml(dirty)` (the `sanitize-html` package's bare-function default export, no `.sanitize` receiver). > `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:6` documents that it deliberately avoids `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` entirely, so the repo has no live instance to calibrate against yet. Both rules declare `languages: [typescript]`. Whether semgrep's `typescript` target reliably parses `.tsx` in the version CodeRabbit runs is **something I could not determine from this repo** — the ast-grep rules alongside them explicitly declare `language: tsx`, which suggests the distinction was considered there and not here. Worth an empirical check before relying on either rule to cover component files. --- ## 4. Git hooks — prevention vs. best-effort Managed by Husky v9 via `"prepare": "husky"` (`package.json:52`). The `.husky/*` files are one-line delegators: `.husky/pre-commit:1` → `bash scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, `.husky/commit-msg:1` → `bash scripts/hooks/commit-msg "$1"`, `.husky/pre-push:1` → `bash scripts/hooks/pre-push`. **`pre-commit`** (`scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, 324 lines) does five things: 1. Resolves `node` through nvm/fnm/volta, hard-fails if absent (`:22-42`). 2. Regenerates `.claude/registry/` and auto-stages it when `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}` or `routes.tsx` is staged (`:49-62`). 3. Regenerates derived AI-config files via `syncCursorRules.mjs --fix` and auto-stages them when a `.claude/rules/*.md` or `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` is staged; **blocks** on failure (`:71-87`). Warns (does not block) when a SKILL.md changes without `.claude/skills/README.md` also staged, plus a Confluence reminder (`:97-118`). 4. Regenerates Contentful `definitions.ts` from staged `experiences/*.tsx` and **blocks** on codegen failure (`:126-160`). 5. **Blocks** direct edits to derived config (`.cursor/rules/`, `.vscode/instructions/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`) when the `.claude/` source isn't co-staged (`:171-250`), and **blocks** `.env.sample` commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value or the value looks like a JWT / 32+ hex / 40+ base64 / a known provider prefix (`:264-322`). > **What `pre-commit` does NOT do: it runs no lint, no `tsc`, and no tests.** Nothing local checks that your code compiles before it becomes a commit. **`commit-msg`** (`scripts/hooks/commit-msg`) — blocks anything not matching `^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$` (`:17`), with a pass-through for `Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP` (`:10-12`). Scope must be lowercase — `feat(ProductTile):` is rejected. Subject capped at 100 chars. **`pre-push`** (`scripts/hooks/pre-push`) — rejects malformed `v*` tags, allowing only `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` (`:20-21`). Keys on the **remote** ref, so `git push origin branch:refs/tags/vX` is also caught (`:16-17`); skips deletions (`:28`). Its own header (`:4-7`) is candid: on the Team plan ruleset `tag_name_pattern` is Enterprise-only, so **this hook is the primary prevention** and `tag-validate.yml` is post-hoc detection only. Non-`v*` tags and all branch pushes pass untouched — **`pre-push` runs no tests, lint, or type-check.** **Bypass:** every one of these is defeated by `git commit --no-verify` / `git push --no-verify`, by `npm install --ignore-scripts` (Husky never installs), or by a fresh clone where `prepare` didn't run. `scripts/hooks/README.md:19-21` states hooks should not be bypassed and points at AGENTS.md hard rule 13. **All three are best-effort, none are prevention.** The only hook whose bypass has no server-side backstop is `pre-push` — CodeRabbit checks commit format at PR time (`coderabbit.yaml:129-135`), and CI can't un-push a bad tag. **Separate layer — Claude Code's own hooks** (`.claude/settings.json`): a `PreToolUse` hook blocks Write/Edit on `develop`/`main` (`:9`), `tier2Warn.sh` warns non-blockingly (`:13`), a `PostToolUse` Prettier format-on-Write (`:24`), plus `contentfulDriftWarn.sh`, `registryUpdate.sh`, `testFileRemind.sh`. All four helper scripts exist in `.claude/hooks/`. These govern only what Claude does — they are invisible to a human editing in an IDE. --- ## 5. `protected-file-guard.yml` and the tier system Trigger: `pull_request` to `develop`, `main`, `release/**`; types `opened, synchronize, reopened` (`:8-13`). - **`tier1-guard` — "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"** (`:39`). What bites you — ten traps **1. A docs-only final commit turns both required checks green. This already happened.** `qa.yml:72` diffs against the previous push, not the merge base. On PR #59 the last commit was `604ece54 docs: reconcile the bootstrap docs...`, and `gh pr checks 59` shows the final state: `Unit tests (Vitest) — skipping`, `Storybook interaction & a11y tests — skipping`, `Playwright E2E (localhost) — skipping`, `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) — skipping`. A PR that rewrote the entire footer merged with **both required test gates reporting skipped-as-passing** on the merged SHA. The `qa.yml:66-71` comment argues this is safe because "nothing relevant changed since the last time those suites ran" — but that reasoning silently assumes the earlier run *passed*. **If a push fails unit tests and you then push a docs-only commit, the required check flips to green.** As a lead: read the *history* of check runs on a PR, not the current state, and treat "skipping" on the head SHA as "unverified," not "passed." **2. `detect-changes` failing green-lights the PR.** Both required test jobs carry `needs: detect-changes` plus a plain `if:` (`qa.yml:210-211`, `:239-240`), so GitHub's implicit `success()` over `needs` applies. If `detect-changes` fails — a `tj-actions/changed-files` hiccup, a filename with shell metacharacters, a `git fetch` failure at `qa.yml:190-194` — both jobs skip, and skipped required checks pass (`qa.yml:22`). The single most load-bearing job in the pipeline is not itself a required check. **3. A header-only change gets the *narrowest* E2E scope despite the *widest* blast radius.** `e2e_homepage` (`qa.yml:97-102`) includes `overrides/app/components/header/**`. The subset check at `qa.yml:139-146` narrows to `--grep "@homepage"` when every changed file is in that list. So a PR touching only the global header — Tier 2, renders on every page — runs *only* homepage E2E. Checkout, PDP, and account journeys never execute. (And E2E isn't a required check anyway, so it's a warning-of-a-warning.) **4. `main` has no test gate, and `Branch Target Check` barely checks anything.** `main` requires exactly one status: `🔴 Branch Target Check`, whose entire assertion is `base == main && head == feature/*` (`protected-file-guard.yml:165`). A `fix/*` branch targeting `main` directly passes it. A `release/*` or `hotfix/*` → `main` passes trivially. Combined with `dismissesStaleReviews: false` and `requireLastPushApproval: false` on `main`, you can secure an approval and then push anything before merging. **5. `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.json`, and `globalStyles.ts` are declared protected and are enforced nowhere.** `frozenFiles.md` calls the first two Tier 1 Build Pipeline; `protectedFiles.md` calls the third Tier 2. None appear in CODEOWNERS, and CODEOWNERS has no catch-all. **`.claude/rules/` is documentation, not configuration** — the tier a file *is* equals the tier CODEOWNERS says it is. When onboarding, teach people to check `CODEOWNERS`, not `frozenFiles.md`, if they want to know what will actually block. **6. `chore(deps): …` in a PR title switches CodeRabbit off entirely.** `coderabbit.yaml:391-393` sets `ignore_title_keywords: ["chore(deps)", "dependabot"]`. Title-matched, not author-matched — so a human PR titled `chore(deps): bump the thing` gets **no CodeRabbit review at all**, including no semgrep, no ast-grep, no gitleaks. Combined with `drafts: false` (`:389`), a PR that stays in draft is also never reviewed. Neither state is visible as a failing check; it just looks quiet. **7. The semgrep XSS rule flags the *correct* pattern and misses the dangerous one.** `semgrep.yml:35` only excludes an **inline** `$SANITIZER.sanitize(...)`. The idiomatic `const clean = DOMPurify.sanitize(dirty)` followed by `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: clean}}` is reported as an ERROR. Meanwhile a spread-props form evades the rule completely, and any object with a no-op `.sanitize()` method satisfies the exclusion. Expect your team to learn to ignore this rule — which is precisely how a real finding gets waved through. Per AGENTS.md's CodeRabbit-reply rule, when you dismiss one of these, **reply in-thread explaining why**, or CodeRabbit re-raises it forever. **8. The `aria-labelledby` false positive.** `icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml:14`'s `^aria-label\b` does not match `aria-labelledby` (word boundary fails on the following `l`). A correctly-labelled IconButton using `aria-labelledby` is reported as an accessibility violation. Same family of problem as #7 — the rule punishes the more sophisticated correct answer. **9. The only a11y gate is a Storybook job that skips on a util change.** `storybook-test` (`qa.yml:236`) is the sole automated WCAG check on a PR, and its trigger path list (`qa.yml:80-88`) omits `overrides/app/utils/**` and `overrides/app/config/**`. Combined with trap #1, a11y coverage is conditional on your last commit's file paths. And per `.claude/rules/testing.md`, `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest, so icon-consuming components must be mocked in unit tests too — meaning neither layer reliably exercises them. **10. `e2e-browserstack` burns paid sessions on cancelled runs, and its comment says otherwise.** `qa.yml:433` uses `always()`; `qa.yml:314` uses `!cancelled()`. The comment at `qa.yml:431` claims they're the same. `e2e-localhost`'s comment (`:309-312`) explains that `!cancelled()` was chosen deliberately so a superseded push doesn't burn a runner slot. BrowserStack — the one that costs real money per session — didn't get the fix. Worth a one-line PR, though note `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 and needs a code-owner review. --- ## Could not determine - **Whether semgrep's `languages: [typescript]` (`semgrep.yml:6`, `:29`) covers `.tsx` in the version CodeRabbit runs.** The sibling ast-grep rules all declare `language: tsx` explicitly, which suggests the distinction mattered there.
